adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, the client always shows a generic success toast (`showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")`) on mutation success. On the server, `addGuests.handler.ts` filters out blacklisted emails and emails already present on the booking (`uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)`), and proceeds successfully as long as at least one email remains, without returning which emails were actually added. This can mislead the user when they submit a mixed list (some dropped, some added). However, the finding overstates it (“toast ... for every submitted email”): there is only one toast per submission, and the system still behaves correctly by adding allowed guests; it’s primarily a UX/feedback completeness issue rather than a functional defect.
